stem:
Reorganize the following food chain. Describe the ecosystem to which it belongs.

Grasshopper – Snake – Paddy field – Eagle – Frog.
Explain the statement- ‘we have got this Earth planet on lease from our future generations and not as an ancestral property from our ancestors.’

note: The chapter NEVER describes the Chipko Movement and never mentions the Bishnoi at all. 'Chipko' occurs exactly twice in the whole chapter: once in a 'Let's Discuss' activity box on printed p41 that says 'Collect the information about Chipko Movement and discuss between two groups of your class about its importance in present situation', and once as 'Chipko Centre, Tehri Garhwal' in the Voluntary Organizations list on printed p43. 'Bishnoi' appears nowhere in the chapter body — its only occurrence in the whole chapter is inside this exercise question. So the book sets a short note on material it deliberately left as an outside-reading activity.

The word 'disaster' occurs NOWHERE in this chapter except inside this exercise question — verified against the full text layer of all eleven pages (PDF idx 45-55). Disaster management is the subject of a SEPARATE chapter of this same volume (Science and Technology Part II, ch.10 'Disaster Management', printed pp 109-120). So this sub-item points outside its own chapter.

stem: How will you justify that overcoming the pollution is a powerful way of environmental management?
Which projects will you run in relation to environmental conservation? How?
Why does the human beings have important place in environment?
note: Ungrammatical as printed ('Why does the human beings have'). Transcribed exactly as it appears on printed p46.

stem: Write the types and examples of biodiversity.
How the biodiversity can be conserved?
What do we learn from the story of Jadav Molai Peyang?
note: The exercise spells the surname 'Peyang'; the chapter's own story box on printed p42 spells it 'Payeng' ('Jadav Molai Payeng is a highly capable person in Assam'). The book is internally inconsistent. The stem is transcribed exactly as printed in the exercise.

stem: Write the names of biodiversity hot spots.
note: The chapter's own 'Hotspots of Biodiversity' section (printed p44) NAMES NO HOTSPOT. It gives only counts and percentages — 34 spots worldwide, once 15.7% of the Earth, 86% already destroyed, 2.3% left, 1,50,000 plant species = 50% of the world count; for India, 85 of 135 animal species in the jungles of the eastern region and about 1,500 endemic plant species in the western ghat — and then instructs the student: 'Collect more information about locations of these hotspots present in the world.' So the book asks for a list it never prints.

stem: Which are the reasons for endangering the many species of plants and animals? How can we save those?
note: BOOK DEFECT — Q6 prints TWO consecutive sub-items both labelled 'f.' (there is no 'g.'), confirmed on the rendered page image of printed p46: 'f. Write the names of biodiversity hot spots.' is immediately followed by 'f. Which are the reasons for endangering...'. The printed label is preserved in the stem's own position in the set; the ref is suffixed '-2' only because a ref must be unique within the chapter (buildRecords throws on a duplicate).

stem: What are the meanings of following symbols? Write your role accordingly?
note: Figure-dependent: three symbols are printed directly under the stem in the right column of printed p46 and the stem points at nothing without them, so the strip is attached as image_url (see data/sci-environment-10.fig.json). The chapter never prints the meaning of any symbol: its own 'Enlist and discuss' box on printed p43 shows four DIFFERENT symbols and likewise only asks the student to 'Find the meaning of those symbols in relation to environment conservation'.
